1→# Shopify App Template - React Router
     2→
     3→This is a template for building a [Shopify app](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/getting-started) using [React Router](https://reactrouter.com/). It was forked from the [Shopify Remix app template](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix) and converted to React Router.
     4→
     5→Rather than cloning this repo, follow the [Quick Start steps](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router#quick-start).
     6→
     7→Visit the [`shopify.dev` documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) for more details on the React Router app package.
     8→
     9→## Upgrading from Remix
    10→
    11→If you have an existing Remix app that you want to upgrade to React Router, please follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/wiki/Upgrading-from-Remix). Otherwise, please follow the quick start guide below.
    12→
    13→## Quick start
    14→
    15→### Prerequisites
    16→
    17→Before you begin, you'll need to [download and install the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/getting-started) if you haven't already.
    18→
    19→### Setup
    20→
    21→```shell
    22→shopify app init --template=https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router
    23→```
    24→
    25→### Local Development
    26→
    27→```shell
    28→shopify app dev
    29→```
    30→
    31→Press P to open the URL to your app. Once you click install, you can start development.
    32→
    33→Local development is powered by [the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli). It logs into your account, connects to an app, provides environment variables, updates remote config, creates a tunnel and provides commands to generate extensions.
    34→
    35→### Authenticating and querying data
    36→
    37→To authenticate and query data you can use the `shopify` const that is exported from `/app/shopify.server.js`:
    38→
    39→```js
    40→export async function loader({ request }) {
    41→  const { admin } = await shopify.authenticate.admin(request);
    42→
    43→  const response = await admin.graphql(`
    44→    {
    45→      products(first: 25) {
    46→        nodes {
    47→          title
    48→          description
    49→        }
    50→      }
    51→    }`);
    52→
    53→  const {
    54→    data: {
    55→      products: { nodes },
    56→    },
    57→  } = await response.json();
    58→
    59→  return nodes;
    60→}
    61→```
    62→
    63→This template comes pre-configured with examples of:
    64→
    65→1. Setting up your Shopify app in [/app/shopify.server.ts](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/shopify.server.ts)
    66→2. Querying data using Graphql. Please see: [/app/routes/app.\_index.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/app._index.tsx).
    67→3. Responding to webhooks. Please see [/app/routes/webhooks.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx).
    68→4. Using metafields, metaobjects, and declarative custom data definitions. Please see [/app/routes/app.\_index.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/app._index.tsx) and [shopify.app.toml](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/shopify.app.toml).
    69→
    70→Please read the [documentation for @shopify/shopify-app-react-router](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) to see what other API's are available.
    71→
    72→## Shopify Dev MCP
    73→
    74→This template is configured with the Shopify Dev MCP. This instructs [Cursor](https://cursor.com/), [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) and [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and [Google Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) to use the Shopify Dev MCP.
    75→
    76→For more information on the Shopify Dev MCP please read [the documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/devmcp).
    77→
    78→## Deployment
    79→
    80→### Application Storage
    81→
    82→This template uses [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io/) to store session data, by default using an [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html) database.
    83→The database is defined as a Prisma schema in `prisma/schema.prisma`.
    84→
    85→This use of SQLite works in production if your app runs as a single instance.
    86→The database that works best for you depends on the data your app needs and how it is queried.
    87→Here’s a short list of databases providers that provide a free tier to get started:
    88→
    89→| Database   | Type             | Hosters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
    90→| ---------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    91→| MySQL      | SQL              | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-mysql), [Planet Scale](https://planetscale.com/), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Google Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql) |
    92→| PostgreSQL | SQL              | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-postgresql), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Google Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres)                                   |
    93→| Redis      | Key-value        | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-redis), [Amazon MemoryDB](https://aws.amazon.com/memorydb/)                                                                                                        |
    94→| MongoDB    | NoSQL / Document | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-mongodb), [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas/database)                                                                                                  |
    95→
    96→To use one of these, you can use a different [datasource provider](https://www.prisma.io/docs/reference/api-reference/prisma-schema-reference#datasource) in your `schema.prisma` file, or a different [SessionStorage adapter package](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-api-js/blob/main/packages/shopify-api/docs/guides/session-storage.md).
    97→
    98→### Build
    99→
   100→Build the app by running the command below with the package manager of your choice:
   101→
   102→Using yarn:
   103→
   104→```shell
   105→yarn build
   106→```
   107→
   108→Using npm:
   109→
   110→```shell
   111→npm run build
   112→```
   113→
   114→Using pnpm:
   115→
   116→```shell
   117→pnpm run build
   118→```
   119→
   120→## Hosting
   121→
   122→When you're ready to set up your app in production, you can follow [our deployment documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment) to host it externally. From there, you have a few options:
   123→
   124→- [Google Cloud Run](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment/deploy-to-google-cloud-run): This tutorial is written specifically for this example repo, and is compatible with the extended steps included in the subsequent [**Build your app**](tutorial) in the **Getting started** docs. It is the most detailed tutorial for taking a React Router-based Shopify app and deploying it to production. It includes configuring permissions and secrets, setting up a production database, and even hosting your apps behind a load balancer across multiple regions.
   125→- [Fly.io](https://fly.io/docs/js/shopify/): Leverages the Fly.io CLI to quickly launch Shopify apps to a single machine.
   126→- [Render](https://render.com/docs/deploy-shopify-app): This tutorial guides you through using Docker to deploy and install apps on a Dev store.
   127→- [Manual deployment guide](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment/deploy-to-hosting-service): This resource provides general guidance on the requirements of deployment including environment variables, secrets, and persistent data.
   128→
   129→When you reach the step for [setting up environment variables](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/deployment/web#set-env-vars), you also need to set the variable `NODE_ENV=production`.
   130→
   131→## Gotchas / Troubleshooting
   132→
   133→### Database tables don't exist
   134→
   135→If you get an error like:
   136→
   137→```
   138→The table `main.Session` does not exist in the current database.
   139→```
   140→
   141→Create the database for Prisma. Run the `setup` script in `package.json` using `npm`, `yarn` or `pnpm`.
   142→
   143→### Navigating/redirecting breaks an embedded app
   144→
   145→Embedded apps must maintain the user session, which can be tricky inside an iFrame. To avoid issues:
   146→
   147→1. Use `Link` from `react-router` or `@shopify/polaris`. Do not use `<a>`.
   148→2. Use `redirect` returned from `authenticate.admin`. Do not use `redirect` from `react-router`
   149→3. Use `useSubmit` from `react-router`.
   150→
   151→This only applies if your app is embedded, which it will be by default.
   152→
   153→### Webhooks: shop-specific webhook subscriptions aren't updated
   154→
   155→If you are registering webhooks in the `afterAuth` hook, using `shopify.registerWebhooks`, you may find that your subscriptions aren't being updated.
   156→
   157→Instead of using the `afterAuth` hook declare app-specific webhooks in the `shopify.app.toml` file. This approach is easier since Shopify will automatically sync changes every time you run `deploy` (e.g: `npm run deploy`). Please read these guides to understand more:
   158→
   159→1. [app-specific vs shop-specific webhooks](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe#app-specific-subscriptions)
   160→2. [Create a subscription tutorial](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe/get-started?deliveryMethod=https)
   161→
   162→If you do need shop-specific webhooks, keep in mind that the package calls `afterAuth` in 2 scenarios:
   163→
   164→- After installing the app
   165→- When an access token expires
   166→
   167→During normal development, the app won't need to re-authenticate most of the time, so shop-specific subscriptions aren't updated. To force your app to update the subscriptions, uninstall and reinstall the app. Revisiting the app will call the `afterAuth` hook.
   168→
   169→### Webhooks: Admin created webhook failing HMAC validation
   170→
   171→Webhooks subscriptions created in the [Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/orders/notifications/webhooks) will fail HMAC validation. This is because the webhook payload is not signed with your app's secret key.
   172→
   173→The recommended solution is to use [app-specific webhooks](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe#app-specific-subscriptions) defined in your toml file instead. Test your webhooks by triggering events manually in the Shopify admin(e.g. Updating the product title to trigger a `PRODUCTS_UPDATE`).
   174→
   175→### Webhooks: Admin object undefined on webhook events triggered by the CLI
   176→
   177→When you trigger a webhook event using the Shopify CLI, the `admin` object will be `undefined`. This is because the CLI triggers an event with a valid, but non-existent, shop. The `admin` object is only available when the webhook is triggered by a shop that has installed the app. This is expected.
   178→
   179→Webhooks triggered by the CLI are intended for initial experimentation testing of your webhook configuration. For more information on how to test your webhooks, see the [Shopify CLI documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/commands#webhook-trigger).
   180→
   181→### Incorrect GraphQL Hints
   182→
   183→By default the [graphql.vscode-graphql](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GraphQL.vscode-graphql) extension for will assume that GraphQL queries or mutations are for the [Shopify Admin API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin). This is a sensible default, but it may not be true if:
   184→
   185→1. You use another Shopify API such as the storefront API.
   186→2. You use a third party GraphQL API.
   187→
   188→If so, please update [.graphqlrc.ts](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/.graphqlrc.ts).
   189→
   190→### Using Defer & await for streaming responses
   191→
   192→By default the CLI uses a cloudflare tunnel. Unfortunately cloudflare tunnels wait for the Response stream to finish, then sends one chunk. This will not affect production.
   193→
   194→To test [streaming using await](https://reactrouter.com/api/components/Await#await) during local development we recommend [localhost based development](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/cli-for-apps/networking-options#localhost-based-development).
   195→
   196→### "nbf" claim timestamp check failed
   197→
   198→This is because a JWT token is expired. If you are consistently getting this error, it could be that the clock on your machine is not in sync with the server. To fix this ensure you have enabled "Set time and date automatically" in the "Date and Time" settings on your computer.
   199→
   200→### Using MongoDB and Prisma
   201→
   202→If you choose to use MongoDB with Prisma, there are some gotchas in Prisma's MongoDB support to be aware of. Please see the [Prisma SessionStorage README](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shopify/shopify-app-session-storage-prisma#mongodb).
   203→
   204→### Unable to require(`C:\...\query_engine-windows.dll.node`).
   205→
   206→Unable to require(`C:\...\query_engine-windows.dll.node`).
   207→The Prisma engines do not seem to be compatible with your system.
   208→
   209→query_engine-windows.dll.node is not a valid Win32 application.
   210→
   211→**Fix:** Set the environment variable:
   212→
   213→```shell
   214→PRISMA_CLIENT_ENGINE_TYPE=binary
   215→```
   216→
   217→This forces Prisma to use the binary engine mode, which runs the query engine as a separate process and can work via emulation on Windows ARM64.
